# Techniques

| name | summary |
|---|---|
| [3D Gaussian Splatting](gaussian-splatting.md) | Scenes are represented as millions of anisotropic 3D Gaussians optimized from photos and rasterized in real time, giving photoreal captured or generated environments at 1080p and 30+ fps. |
| [Agent-based automated playtesting and balancing](automated-playtesting.md) | Studios train imitation, reinforcement learning, and search agents to play builds, estimating level difficulty, pass and churn rates, progression pacing, map coverage, and exploits before players reach them. |
| [Automated generation of game rules and mechanics](automated-rule-generation.md) | Systems that write complete game rule sets as code in a description language, using evolution or language models to propose rules and self-play agents to score balance, decisiveness, and strategic depth before a human sees them. |
| [Continuous cellular automata and foundation-model search for artificial life](continuous-alife-and-asal.md) | Continuous cellular automata such as Lenia and mass-conserving Flow-Lenia produce lifelike self-organizing creatures, and ASAL uses vision-language foundation models to search their rule spaces for phenomena described in text or for open-ended novelty. |
| [Deep reinforcement learning policies for NPC opponents and navigation](deep-rl-npc-policies.md) | Neural control policies trained with deep reinforcement learning inside the game's own simulation drive opponents and NPCs, as with Sony AI's Gran Turismo Sophy, a selectable rival in Gran Turismo 7 since 2023. |
| [Differentiable simulation](differentiable-simulation.md) | Simulators written so automatic differentiation returns gradients of an outcome with respect to initial state, controls, or rule parameters, replacing black-box search with gradient descent for tuning and inverse design. |
| [Diffusion and autoregressive neural game engines](diffusion-game-engines.md) | Action-conditioned generative models trained on recordings of one existing game predict each next frame from recent frames and player input, so the model itself plays the role of the game engine. |
| [Generalist instructable game agents (SIMA)](generalist-game-agents.md) | Agents that read screen pixels and natural-language instructions and output keyboard and mouse actions across many commercial 3D games, with later versions reasoning, conversing, and improving through self-generated tasks. |
| [Generative agents (memory stream, reflection, planning)](generative-agents.md) | LLM-driven characters that store observations in a natural-language memory stream, retrieve them by recency, importance, and relevance, synthesize reflections, and plan their day top-down. |
| [Genie foundation world models](genie-world-models.md) | Google DeepMind's Genie models generate playable worlds from a text or image prompt and render them in real time from player input, with Genie 3 reaching 720p at 24 fps and about a minute of visual memory. |
| [Grammar-constrained decoding for valid game actions](constrained-decoding.md) | Decoding that masks every token which cannot extend a valid string of a schema, regular expression, or grammar, so a model's output always parses as a legal game action or data record. |
| [Graph network simulators and neural operators](graph-network-simulators.md) | Learned simulators that predict the next state of particles, meshes, or continuous fields with message-passing networks or Fourier-space operators, trained on numerical solver output and run 10-1000x faster than that solver. |
| [Language models grounded in strategic planning for negotiation games](cicero-strategic-dialogue.md) | Meta's Cicero couples a dialogue language model with a planning engine that infers other players' intentions from the board and conversation, so its free-text negotiation proposes and follows concrete joint plans, reaching human-level Diplomacy. |
| [Learned kinematic motion synthesis](learned-motion-synthesis.md) | Neural networks generate or compress kinematic character animation, as in Ubisoft's learned motion matching, EA's HyperMotion, and inZOI's motion extraction from uploaded video. |
| [Learned level and map generation (PCGRL, MarioGPT, LLM generators)](learned-level-generation.md) | Generators trained by reinforcement learning or on example levels, including small and large language models that emit tile maps from text prompts, produce playable levels and maps without hand-written generation rules. |
| [Learned physics-based character control](physics-based-character-control.md) | Neural policies trained with reinforcement learning drive simulated humanoids by joint torques to imitate motion capture, and MaskedMimic-style controllers accept partial goals such as keyframes, text, or an object to sit on. |
| [LLM explanation of simulation state](llm-explanation-of-state.md) | Language models that read simulation state, modifier breakdowns, agent traces, or event logs and answer why and what-if questions or summarize what happened for players and designers. |
| [LLM game master and narrative director](llm-game-master.md) | A language model that adjudicates player and NPC intentions, decides outcomes, generates events and quests, and narrates them, either free-form or checked against a typed world state and canon. |
| [LLM models of individual human choice](human-behavior-simulation-models.md) | Language models conditioned on interviews or fine-tuned on millions of experimental choices that predict how specific people or populations answer surveys, play economic games, and choose in decision tasks. |
| [LLM-adjudicated state transitions (LLM as game mechanic)](llm-rule-adjudication.md) | A language model computes the outcome of an interaction (two elements combined, an action on an object) from a text description of the inputs, with results cached so every player sees the same rule. |
| [LLM-guided evolutionary program search](alphaevolve-algorithm-discovery.md) | An LLM proposes edits to code, an automated evaluator scores each candidate, and an evolutionary database keeps the best and most diverse programs, finding heuristics and constructions that beat human-designed ones. |
| [LLM-written skill libraries (Voyager)](voyager-skill-libraries.md) | An LLM agent that proposes its own next task, writes executable code to do it, refines the code from execution errors and self-checks, and stores verified programs in a retrievable skill library. |
| [Machine-learned weather forecasting](ml-weather-models.md) | Neural networks trained on decades of atmospheric reanalysis forecast global weather 10-15 days ahead in seconds to minutes on one accelerator, matching or beating physics-based operational models on most verification targets. |
| [Many-agent LLM societies](llm-agent-societies.md) | Simulations of hundreds to a million LLM-driven agents with concurrent cognitive modules, shared environments, and message buses that produce role specialization, rule changes, cultural spread, and polarization. |
| [Massively parallel GPU simulation](massively-parallel-simulation.md) | Simulators that keep thousands of world instances as tensors on a GPU or TPU and step them all in one kernel, raising throughput to millions of steps per second for agent training and Monte Carlo sweeps. |
| [Mean field games and mean-field learning](mean-field-games.md) | Mean field game theory replaces an N-player game with one representative agent responding to the population distribution, and recent learning methods compute these equilibria for state spaces of hundreds of billions of states. |
| [ML reconstruction of the planet from aerial imagery](satellite-world-reconstruction.md) | Machine learning classifies buildings, vegetation, and terrain in satellite and aerial imagery and procedural rules rebuild them as 3D scenery, which Microsoft Flight Simulator streams for the whole Earth. |
| [Monte Carlo tree search for game AI](monte-carlo-tree-search.md) | A best-first search that grows a game tree from repeated simulated playouts and picks branches with a bandit rule such as UCT, letting AI players plan from a forward model without a hand-tuned evaluation function. |
| [Muse World and Human Action Model (WHAM)](muse-wham.md) | Microsoft Research's WHAM is a transformer trained on seven years of Bleeding Edge play that generates both future frames and the player's controller actions, aimed at gameplay ideation, with a real-time Quake II follow-up (WHAMM). |
| [Neural cellular automata](neural-cellular-automata.md) | Cellular automata whose local update rule is a small learned network or logic circuit, trained so that cells grow, maintain, and regenerate a target pattern, texture, structure, or level from a seed. |
| [Neural rendering in the graphics pipeline](neural-rendering-shaders.md) | Small neural networks inside the renderer upscale frames, generate extra frames, denoise ray tracing, decode compressed textures and layered materials, and since DLSS 5 re-light the final frame, all without touching simulation state. |
| [On-device small language models for characters](on-device-language-models.md) | Pruned, distilled, and 4-bit quantized language, speech, and embedding models that run on the player's GPU beside rendering to drive character decisions, dialogue, and voice without per-token server cost. |
| [Open real-time interactive video world models](open-interactive-video-models.md) | Open and startup interactive video models (Matrix-Game, Hunyuan-GameCraft, WorldPlay, Yan, Mirage, Odyssey) adapt pretrained video diffusion transformers to keyboard and mouse control and stream frames in real time, adding pose-indexed memory and text edits during play. |
| [Open-ended co-generation of environments and agents](open-ended-environment-generation.md) | Systems that keep generating new environments or tasks at the edge of an agent's ability and train agents on them, from POET's co-evolved terrains to OMNI-EPIC's foundation-model-written task code and SIMA 2 practicing in Genie 3 worlds. |
| [Physical-world foundation models](physical-world-foundation-models.md) | Video-pretrained models of physical dynamics, NVIDIA Cosmos for generating action-conditioned training video and Meta's V-JEPA 2 for latent prediction and planning, target robotics and driving rather than games. |
| [Prompt-to-persistent 3D world generation](generated-3d-worlds.md) | Models such as World Labs Marble and HunyuanWorld turn text, images, video, or coarse 3D blockouts into persistent explorable scenes exported as Gaussian splats and meshes with collision proxies. |
| [Quality-diversity search (MAP-Elites) for content and balance](quality-diversity-search.md) | Evolutionary search that keeps the best solution found in each cell of a grid of designer-chosen behavior descriptors, returning an archive of diverse high-quality levels, decks, or strategies instead of one optimum. |
| [Real-time generative restyling of game video](real-time-video-restyling.md) | A live video-to-video diffusion model repaints each frame of a running game from a text prompt in under 40 ms, leaving the game's own simulation and state untouched. |
| [Realtime speech-to-speech and expressive TTS for characters](realtime-voice-models.md) | Streaming speech recognition, speech-native language models, and context-aware text-to-speech that let characters hold spoken, interruptible conversations with roughly 200-250 ms response onset and generated emotional delivery. |
| [Regret minimization and search for imperfect-information games](imperfect-information-solvers.md) | Self-play algorithms that minimize counterfactual regret over information sets, refined by real-time subgame search, compute hard-to-exploit strategies that bluff and hide information and beat top humans at poker, Stratego, and Scotland Yard. |
| [Self-play planning with learned models (AlphaZero, MuZero, Dreamer)](model-based-planning-muzero.md) | Agents that combine tree search or imagined rollouts with neural policy and value networks trained by self-play, where MuZero and Dreamer also learn the environment's dynamics, reach superhuman play from rules or pixels alone. |
| [Simulation-based inference for calibrating simulators](simulation-based-inference.md) | Neural density estimators trained on simulator runs return a posterior over a simulator's parameters given observed data, calibrating agent-based and economic models whose likelihoods cannot be computed. |
| [Subspace neural physics and learned deformers](subspace-neural-physics.md) | Small networks trained on offline cloth, flesh, or muscle simulation predict deformation in a compressed subspace or as corrective morph targets, running hundreds to thousands of times faster than the source simulation inside a game engine. |
| [Text- and image-to-3D asset generation](text-to-3d-assets.md) | Open 3D generative models (TRELLIS, Hunyuan3D 2.x, Roblox Cube) produce textured meshes from a text prompt or image in seconds to a minute, and inZOI exposes image-to-3D object creation to players. |
| [Wave Function Collapse and constraint-based tile generation](wave-function-collapse.md) | An example-driven constraint solver that fills a grid by repeatedly collapsing the lowest-entropy cell to one tile and propagating adjacency constraints, shipped in games including Townscaper, Bad North, and Caves of Qud. |
